note: The hand-kept map behind the generated progress view (rule I, 2026-11-17): which experiments and hypotheses belong to which scope, and the dated hand-written context. build_research.py writes progress/README.md and the S files from this map and the data record; every experiment must sit in exactly one scope or the build stops.
intro:
Owner instruction (2026-11-06, in the lab session): work like a research team following a scientific procedure, keep a
progress document per scope the owner can read, and use deep search when the question is "what others have done so
far". The procedure the lab follows, per scope:

1. Observe: what is going on in the roadmap, the repositories, the architecture and the PRs, and why this scope matters now.
2. Hypothesise: what could be done for better performance, accuracy, assurance or cost (the register's H-rows).
3. Collect: the data the hypothesis needs, from the platform's own records, the repositories' exports and the literature
   (digest-pinned; outside sources through deep search, recorded with their identifiers).
4. Design and test: a preregistration, an independent review of it, the run, a verdict in the ledger form.
5. Report and prove: a one-page report with what was measured, what it means and what it does not show; proposals to the
   roadmap visionary through the lane monitor.

scopes.title: S1: the history chain and the cost of re-proving everything
scopes.question: How much does re-proving the whole history cost, and what does the signed checkpoint buy?

reading.observe: Every harness-onion packet re-executes the whole accepted history (92 layers at slot 280) on every verify. Verify time reached the owner's 1,000 s floor and the 1,200 s cap (slots 272-280: 956 to 1,162 s); the owner adopted eight workers (PERF-046) and chose the signed checkpoint with sampled re-execution (CHAIN-COMPACTION-002, G1) with four conditions; a fifth, shadow mode, was the lab's to rule on. Why now: the cap is the programme's hardest number and every contract packet pays it.
reading.data: The verifier's masked run records (27 runs, PRs 207-232) and the merge-decision rows (RL-01); the cost split at 280 (R00's cost_split280, 11 lines); the architecture export at afee03b9 (RL-07: identity rule, vectors); DESIGN_CC2 rev 2 (R00, read masked).
reading.results: Load drives verify time (about 25-50 s per unit of run-mean load); growth at equal load is 9.3 s per slot (interval 5.7 to 13.5), reproducing the report's 13 s within the band; the attested share of argv 63 is 0.645 and a 10 percent sample keeps argv 63 near 220 s with an expected defect-detection delay of 6.5 verifies and a hard bound of 10 at cadence 10; the chain vectors replay exactly; cost is spread, not concentrated (Gini about 0.5; argv 63 is 0.86 of CPU). Verdicts: RL-01 PASS by gate (H-07a), RL-07 PASS, RL-08 UNRESOLVED (no refusal history), RL-16 PASS.
reading.next: H-02's shadow half when MET-PERF-047's first shadow verify exists (the measured per-layer seconds and the sample's agreement replace the proportional bound); an Ekstazi-style file-dependency arm as a comparison, named for R00.

scopes.title: S2: review independence, the merge predicate and the programme's own process
scopes.question: Do reviews, the oracle and the verifier find different things, and does the programme's own process leave a measurable trace?

reading.observe: Every merge rests on independent review rounds, an owner-held verifier and head-bound approval; the programme records every decision and every monitor rule in dated handoff files. Why now: the custody model is the programme's A2 differentiator and its evidence lives only in these records.
reading.data: Merge-decision records and review records through the masking reader; the verifier's refusals after PASS_FOR_PUSH; the lanes' handoff files (40 resume blocks); the dated MON rules (1,012 identifiers).
reading.results: The process is measurable from its records; the predicate holds from 2026-10-24; finding identity across rounds and an oracle record do not exist yet, so review independence cannot be measured until REVIEW-RECORD-SERIES-001 lands; pinning in resume blocks does not predict fewer rules.
reading.next: H-09 and H-32 when the review-record series gives finding identity; a text-level rule taxonomy on the monitor's permission; the "correlated-error floor" (same model family for author and reviewer) as a column.

scopes.title: S3: the multi-agent coordination contracts
scopes.question: Are the multi-agent contracts (topology, board, run manifest, ledgers) correct, replayable and implementable by another runtime?

reading.observe: The platform's multi-agent runtime is contracts first: TopologySpec and the coordinator board (MAS-RA-004), the run manifest and distribution gate (MAS-RA-002), the verdict ledger (MAS-RA-001), run events (MAS-RA-003), and the conformance labs' simulation campaigns (CONF-MAS-001..005) with their ledgers. Why now: the literature says more agents often hurt; the contracts bound topology by design; whether they are correct, replayable and implementable by others decides B3's publishability and the admission gate.
reading.data: The conformance-labs export at b4bbea79 (the harness, 13 classes, 32 seeds, ledgers); harness-onion's architecture at afee03b9 and c1b838be (records, schemas, 85 + 95 vectors, 114 authority records).
reading.results: The contracts are deterministic, their vectors reproduce from the records alone, and two of them have been re-implemented clean-room; replay safety rests on durable state, not the event log; the paired gate and per-class bounds answer different questions; a simulation has no token budget.
reading.next: The mid-run stale-version vector (R12); the fault-class half of H-27 (DATA-CORRECTNESS-001); the strategy envelope when its record exists; the authority map from the creator-and-basis graph.

scopes.title: S4: host enforcement completeness and the evidence algebra
scopes.question: Is the host's enforcement complete and is its evidence one algebra?

reading.observe: The native profile composes seccomp allowlists, a SELinux matrix, descriptor sets and T04 proofs per role, with gate-channel contracts beside them; Alpha 2 waits on native Linux qualification. Why now: the literature says the primitives are mature and the risk is compositional completeness.
reading.data: The architecture export at afee03b9: allowlists, matrix, host-interface amendments, threat statements, the verdict-ledger and native-profile records; the visionary's coverage cells; R10's cited transcripts.
reading.results: Coverage is nearly complete where the records enumerate paths, and the gap is enumeration itself (counterexamples 1-17); the evidence algebra holds per claim with one five-level order and total maps.
reading.next: A host-interface amendment that enumerates paths 1-17 (named for R10 through the monitor); the first native run as the case study (H-20) when CONF-LINUX-001 exists.

scopes.title: S5: the programme's planning and literature records as checkable data
scopes.question: Can the programme's planning and literature records be checked by script?

reading.observe: The roadmap is a scored JSON record built by script with validators; the research crosswalk pins papers and figures by digest; outside syntheses report figures the programme repeats. Why now: these records are the programme's memory, and a wrong figure or an unchecked status travels.
reading.data: A pristine copy of roadmap/ at fce8245b (never the bridge's own); the five papers the owner approved, held by digest; the three owner-supplied syntheses.
reading.results: The roadmap build refuses what it can see in one file and not what needs a second record or a digest check; the syntheses' figures hold except one shared misreading.
reading.next: The two validators if the visionary takes them; a space-aware extractor for a wider figure check.

scopes.title: S6: what others have done, and what it changes here
scopes.question: What have others done, and what does it change in our hypotheses?

reading.observe: The owner supplied three outside syntheses (RS-1 61fa9041, RS-2 5b30977b, RS-3 930f89a0) over the programme's R&D report, with streams, scores, decision gates and literature; the owner approved five papers for fetching and permits deep search for this question from 2026-11-06.
reading.hypotheses: The three independence variables for review (custody, context, model family); the configuration tuple as the unit of evaluation and the precision-optimal repeat count; the 45 percent single-agent threshold and the linear coordination predictor for topology choice; AgentLTL's three constraint types for gate interleaving; MPBench's write channels for memory; shadow-first compaction and routing.
reading.data: Held and read: Agentproof (arXiv 2603.20356), Harness-Bench (2605.27922), the repeated-running paper (2606.00920), the Nature Machine Intelligence collaboration study (DOI 10.1038/s42256-026-01268-y), the memory poisoning study (2606.04329). Not held: the oversight study (a challenge page; never retried). Second tier (MAS-ProVe 2602.03053, VeriHarness 2610.00972, AgentLTL 2607.02599, SAFER 2510.10193, Styx, Ekstazi, LDFI, the PREreview): identifiers on record, owner "Not now".
reading.experiments: The three design reads (RD-ROADMAP-LAB-READ v2; RD-ACADEMIC-PAPERS-LAB-READ); RL-19's figure check.
reading.results: The syntheses agree on streams, the 60/25/15 split, shadow-first compaction and the configuration tuple; their scores are advisory beside ours; 28 of 29 of their figures hold; four register hypotheses (H-32..H-35) and three candidate classes came from them.
reading.next: Deep search per scope when a hypothesis needs "what others have done": the first asks are the coordination-contract literature (interchange formats for agent assurance; replay via durable state) and the checkpoint-sampling literature (regression test selection with safety bounds); each source recorded by identifier and digest, each fetch reported to the monitor.
